Senses.Explanation: Literally, transmit the lamp. The expression uses one lamp lighting the next for continuation from teacher to successor. Records pair it with continuing the flame, say that lamp follows lamp and ancestor transmits to ancestor, and ask what is being continued. The preface to the Jingde Record explicitly calls it 'the comparison of transmitting the lamp.' A later preface gives its own intensified definition: 'transmitting the lamp is transmitting this hot flame.' That hot-flame equation belongs to that preface's five-lamps discussion and is not imposed on every occurrence.
Senses.Note: Across both senses the headword occurs 982 times in 210 allowlisted texts. The succession formula 'lamp after lamp continues' occurs 71 times in 58 texts; 'continue the flame and transmit the lamp' occurs twice in two texts.

Senses.Explanation: As a title element and shorthand, the compound names the historical lamp-record genre. The headword plus 'record' occurs 382 times in 61 allowlisted texts. The Jingde preface says that a thirty-volume work covering fifty-two generations and 1,701 people was titled the Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp. The Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp uses the same compound in its title. A later discourse enumerates five lamp works by shorthand: Transmission Lamp, Broad Lamp, Universal Lamp, Continued Lamp, and Linked Lamp.
Senses.Note: This bibliographic sense is distinguished because occurrences often refer to a named book or family of records rather than the act of succession. The literal lamp image remains visible in the titles.
